cohort: Pregnant women undergoing planned cesarean delivery
finding: Late-term cesarean delivery was not associated with increased maternal morbidity or general anesthesia rates compared to early-term cesarean delivery, but was associated with higher rates of urgent surgery, spontaneous onset of labor, and out-of-hours surgery.
mod_finding: Late-term cesarean delivery was associated with higher rates of urgent surgery, spontaneous onset of labor, and out-of-hours surgery compared to early-term cesarean delivery.
